title: Client-contract-aware load shift and degradation negotiation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During cross-region overloads and network partitions we currently rely on static priority lanes and coarse admission controllers. This leads to suboptimal behavior for customers with explicit SLA/SLO contracts: some customers are overprotected while others are under-served, and application teams lose the ability to express acceptable graceful degradation modes. Goal: build an extensible negotiation layer that lets the platform use per-tenant contract metadata and per-request hints to (1) shift requests across regions when safe, (2) apply contract-aware fidelity reductions, and (3) coordinate with circuit breakers and admission controllers to minimize customer-visible errors while preserving cluster SLOs.

Approach summary: implement a lightweight handshake + policy chain where the API surface includes standardized contract headers and a Tenant Contract Store. Admission controller queries an augmented policy engine (policy inputs: tenant contract, current SLO burn rates, regional capacity, request affinity) and returns an action (accept, delay-with-grace-window, accept-with-fidelity-reduction, reroute-to-region, reject-with-backoff-suggestion). The runtime applies transformations (structured trimming, token budget capping, model variant fallback) and emits structured traces for observability. The system honors explicit tenant-negotiation flags: preferred_failover_regions, min_fidelity, and emergency_prioritization=true/false.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine honors tenant contract metadata and returns valid actions in 95th percentile < 5ms
Runtime enforces requested fidelity reductions without increasing median tail latency by > 10%
End-to-end can reroute requests to standby region with cached KV when network to primary degrades, verified in chaos tests
Circuit breaker integration prevents rollouts from tripping entire cluster under synthetic overloads in canary runs
New headers and behaviors documented in API spec and test harness added to QA repo
implementation_plan: Design contract schema and request hint headers (RFC draft) -> Confluence link
Prototype policy engine extension (policy inputs, scoring, and action output) as an in-process extension to admission-controller service
Add runtime transforms for fidelity negotiation: structured-field-trim, token-budget-capping, model-variant-mapping
Wire in multi-region handoff path: route decision, KV cache fall-through, and async retry semantics
Integrate with circuit-breaker service so policy engine observes breaker state and can bias decisions
Build unit + integration tests + chaos experiments (partition, regional outage, hit storms)
Incremental rollout: lab -> staging -> canary (5% traffic) -> gradual (25%, 50%) with automatic rollback on SLO regressions
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Tenant metadata staleness leads to wrong decisions. Mitigation: TTL + optimistic refresh + no-op fallback to safe-mode (reject/standard priority)
Risk: Added latency in admission decision. Mitigation: cache recent decisions per-tenant, local LRU with hot-tenant pinning, and degrade to fast path if policy backend slow
Risk: Reroute churn causes cache misses & higher cost. Mitigation: prefer local fidelity transforms before rerouting; use KV cache replication hints and warming
Risk: Complex interactions with existing shedding policies create oscillations. Mitigation: run a policy-emulator on historical traces for stability testing; add hysteresis and backoff windows
metrics_to_monitor: Decision latency P50/P95/P99 for policy engine
SLO burn rate by region and tenant (error budget consumption)
Tail latency delta after applying fidelity transforms
Reroute success rate and cross-region added latency
Circuit breaker trip counts and correlation with policy actions
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy scoring and action output
Integration test: simulated hotspot where primary region overloads and policy selects reroute or fidelity reduction
Chaos test: link partition between region A and B and assert service remains within SLO for VIP tenants with failover enabled
Load test: 3x normal traffic with mixed tenants; verify graceful degradation behavior and absence of global cascading failures
Canary run with 10 internal customers and telemetry dashboards
observability_and_dashboards: New dashboard: Contract-negotiation overview (action heatmap, per-tenant burn)
Alert: policy decision latency > 20ms sustained for 2m
Alert: cross-region reroute rate exceeds threshold correlated with SLO breach
Tracing: attach negotiation decision id to request traces for root-cause analysis
rollout_steps: Lab prototype behind feature flag (runtime & admission-controller) - dev cluster
Staging integration with synthetic traffic and chaos injection
Canary in production with 5% traffic and opt-in tenants
Automated SLO gates: block rollout if regional error budget burned > 10% in 30m
Full rollout with 1-week monitoring window and postmortem review
open_questions: How expressive should tenant contract schema be without becoming an operator burden? (sets vs rate buckets vs per-route flags)
Should policy engine support per-request ML scoring for criticality, or be rule-based initial phase?
How to bill for cross-region reroute costs under dedicated plans? Need PM input
Failure semantics for rerouted requests when target region lacks model variant: retry vs transform vs reject

2026-03-04 - Marcus Nguyen: Prototype policy engine implemented as local extension. Noted decision latency median 3.8ms, P95 18ms on dev. Need to add LRU cache for hot tenants.
2026-03-05 - Elena Garcia (SRE): Reviewed chaos plan. Recommended adding hysteresis window of 60s to avoid route-flapping during transient spikes.
2026-03-07 - Product (Rohit Banerjee): Asked to include billing note for cross-region failover under Dedicated contracts; assigned to PM follow-up.
2026-03-09 - Marcus Nguyen: Added integration tests for token-budget-capping transform. Observed minimal quality degradation on short text prompts in internal evals.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Decided to ship rule-based policy for initial rollout; ML scoring deferred to a later iteration (Q3). Opening ENG-315111 to track ML scoring work.

Add hysteresis/backoff windows to policy engine (SRE pair)
Finalize API header RFC and publish SDK helpers (DX team)
Schedule canary with internal tenants on 2026-03-22
